title: Bootstrap safety layers: k8s on-prem guidance
body:
Purpose:
This is a working guidance doc for adding pragmatic safety layers to on-prem Kubernetes cluster bootstrap and upgrade flows (bare metal and vSphere). Aim: reduce blast radius from bad images/ignition, terraform drift, or operator incompatibilities by layering small, verifiable gates that are easy to run during field ops.

Scope:
- Target: k8s 1.26+ clusters used for Redwood Private deployments (control plane HA, external etcd optional).
- Environments: bare metal (PXE/ignition) and vSphere VM templates.
- Not covered: application-level release processes (we assume app rollout hooks exist).

High-level safety layers (conceptual):
1) Immutable preflight assertions (fast, fail-hard): hardware/VM inventory, firmware/NIC drivers, CPU topology, BIOS flags, time sync check.
2) Deterministic idempotent terraform plan review: small module boundaries, separate state per node-pool and control-plane, plan diffs posted to PRs.
3) Canary seeds: provision 1-2 control-plane nodes + 1 worker with minimal apps; smoke tests run for N hours before fleet-wide rollout.
4) Read-only cluster window for upgrades: network and storage heavy operations blocked for a short maintenance window to avoid cross-impact.
5) Rollback artifacts: preserved etcd snapshots, terraform state backups, and a tested step-by-step rollback playbook per release.

Practical preflight checklist (run locally or from bootstrap control-machine):
- Hardware/VM checks:
  - Verify node BIOS/firmware level: vendor CLI or IPMI output.
  - Confirm CPU flags: virtualization, AES, XSAVE via /proc/cpuinfo.
  - Disk health SMART quick test: smartctl -H /dev/sdX.
- Network checks:
  - MTU consistency between hosts and switches; ip link show dev eth0.
  - Ping gateway, test DNS resolution forward and reverse (dig + dig -x).
  - Verify NAT/firewall rules for control-plane ports (6443 tcp, etcd ports, 2379/2380 if external).
- Time and entropy:
  - timedatectl status; ensure NTP/chrony configured, time drift < 500ms.
  - rngd/avail entropy on VMs.
- Required services/versions:
  - kubelet binary compat, container runtime (containerd) config check.
  - CRI plugin present and compatible with runtimeShim + cgroup driver consistent across nodes.

Terraform module patterns and notes (practical):
- Module boundaries: split infra modules into {control-plane, worker-pool, networking, storage-operator} with separate state files (s3/gcs/remote) to minimize locking during upgrades.
- Inputs: make minimal required inputs; accept a single node_profile object with explicit cpu, mem, disks (avoid templated sizes that hide differences).
- Outputs: expose resource ids, IPs, macs as strings. Keep outputs stable across runs (avoid timestamp prefixes).
- Example snippet (pseudo):
  module "control_plane" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform//modules/control-plane?ref=v1.3.0"
    cluster_name = var.cluster_name
    node_profile = var.cp_profile
    bootstrap_token = var.bootstrap_token
  }
- State locking: use short lock TTL for worker-pool changes; long TTL for control-plane changes.\
- Drift policy: nightly plan-run that posts diffs to a private slack channel and creates JIRA when drift > threshold.

Canary strategy (recommended):
- Phase 0: Create isolated project/namespace with minimal monitoring hooks.
- Phase 1: Provision 1 cp + 1 worker via terraform control-plane module with canary tag.
- Phase 2: Run canonical smoke tests: etcd write/read, kube-proxy basic flows, coredns resolution, PVC create/delete against storage class.
- Phase 3: If green for 2 hours and SLOs within baseline (latency, pod startup), continue staged rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100%.

Upgrade playbook (minor versions and important patch releases):
- Preconditions:
  - All etcd snapshots taken and pushed to backup storage (s3/internal), retention for 7 days for upgrade window.
  - Terraform state snapshot: terraform state pull > state-YYYYMMDD.json, upload to archive bucket.
  - CI smoke tests for the target k8s version run against a simulated environment (local kind or CI infra).
- Steps (control plane first):
  1) Announce maintenance window in #infra-ops (slack) and set cluster label maintenance=true.
  2) Disable automated horizontal scaling and any autoscalers that may react poorly during drain.
  3) Apply control-plane terraform module change to roll to new kubelet/kubeadm image (drain is done manually below):
     - terraform apply on control-plane state only.
  4) For each control-plane node (canary then one-by-one):
     - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=30m
     - System-level: stop kubelet, replace binaries/configs, restart kubelet, validate node Ready.
     - Validate etcd quorum after each node; run etcdctl endpoint status.
  5) After control-plane completes, roll worker pools by node-pool ordering (least critical first):
     - cordon -> drain -> reprovision (or patch in-place) -> uncordon.
- Post-upgrade validation:
  - Run e2e smoke (same as canary) and a longer litmus test for 24h traffic pattern simulation.
  - Check storage operator health (rook/longhorn operator versions), CSI driver logs, and PVC throughput tests.

Rollback plan (triggers and steps):
- Immediate triggers: etcd quorum loss, >20% node NotReady, storage corruption detected, control-plane API errors > 5% 10m.
- Immediate actions:
  1) Pause further rollout and flip cluster label maintenance=false to stop automation.
  2) Restore etcd from most recent snapshot (procedure documented in recovery playbook).
  3) Revert terraform by applying stored state snapshot (terraform import/restore flow) to recreate previous VM images if needed.
  4) If rollback requires re-creating VMs: reprovision control-plane nodes using archived images and terraform state, attach restored etcd.
- Post-rollback: root-cause triage, writeup, and add a blocking JIRA to prevent re-deploy of same change.

Operational guardrails and observability hooks (must be automated where possible):
- Preflight automation: small CLI (bootstrap-check) that runs the preflight checklist and emits JSON with verdict and failure reasons; return non-zero if any fatal issues.
- Alerting: loss of etcd quorum -> PagerDuty; node churn > X/hour -> #infra-ops.
- Health dashboards: per-cluster tiles with control-plane latency, etcd commit latency, core DNS p95, and PVC attach latency.
- Audit: all terraform applies must be linked to PR and have approver for control-plane changes.

Field notes / gotchas we keep seeing:
- vSphere templates with mixed NIC naming cause kubelet network plugin mismatches; enforce template spec with consistent network adapter type and set net.ifnames=0 if needed.
- Ignition vs cloud-init: ignition is deterministic for metal, cloud-init causes non-idempotent user-data actions on firstboot. Prefer ignition for bare metal.
- Time drift on VMs created from templates missing chrony config — include chrony in template.%
- Storage driver upgrades often require CRD changes; validate operator CRDs in canary namespace before cluster upgrade.

TODOs and open questions:
- [ ] Decide exact time drift threshold for gating: 200ms or 500ms? (action: SRE to propose)
- [ ] Add terraform plan diffs posting bot that annotates PRs with human-friendly summary.
- [ ] Validate upgrade path for k8s 1.30 -> 1.31 in our CI.
- [ ] Formalize etcd snapshot retention policy for private customers.

Quick commands (copy/paste helpers):
- etcd snapshot (local urgent): 
  ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 
    --cacert=/etc/etcd/pki/ca.crt --cert=/etc/etcd/pki/peer.crt --key=/etc/etcd/pki/peer.key snapshot save /tmp/etcd-$(date +%F).db
- basic drain + patch: 
  kubectl cordon worker-12
  kubectl drain worker-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --timeout=30m
  ssh ops@worker-12 'sudo systemctl stop kubelet; sudo dpkg -i /tmp/kubelet_1.26.3.deb; sudo systemctl start kubelet'
  kubectl uncordon worker-12

Appendix: minimal playbook for single operator to follow (checklist style):
1) Set maintenance=true label and announce.
2) Run bootstrap-check on each new node (capture output).
3) Take etcd snapshot and upload.
4) Terraform state pull + upload snapshot.
5) Provision canary, run smoke tests 2h.
6) Proceed staged rollout if green.
7) If any critical error, follow rollback plan and invoke oncall.

Notes to self: keep this doc short and focused — link out to recovery-runbook and terraform-module-README for exact commands. Save an example output of bootstrap-check in the infra repo under /examples for quick triage.
